channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Reunião sobre maioridade penal na Câmara mostra PT ainda distante da pauta da segurança pública
item.description: A CCJ meeting on reducing the age of criminal responsibility to 16 showed complete absence of PT deputies, while right-wing legislators attended in force. The only left-wing voice was Talíria Petrone (PSOL-RJ), who unsuccessfully attempted to block the proposal. The Lula government seeks to claim ownership of the public security agenda despite poor evaluations in polls like Datafolha.

item.title: Terceira via tem janela estreita para se viabilizar com discurso anticorrupção
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy faces growing risks from leaked conversations and the erosion of the Bolsonaro brand, opening a narrow window for an anti-corruption 'third way.' Voters, weary of both Lula and the Bolsonaro legacy, are more open to new leadership, though few competitive alternatives have yet emerged. The viability of such a candidate depends on the short campaign period, which only gains broad traction among voters starting in August.

item.title: Corte da Itália conclui julgamento final sobre recurso de Zambelli contra extradição para o Brasil
item.description: Italy's Supreme Court of Cassation ruled on the appeal filed by former deputy Carla Zambelli against her extradition to Brazil. The decision, considered final in the Italian judicial system, will be communicated to her lawyers in the coming hours. The case involves allegations of electoral crimes and abuse of power in Brazil.

item.title: Renan Santos defende processamento de terras-raras no Brasil
item.description: Renan Santos, presidential pre-candidate for the Missão party, argues Brazil should move beyond rare earth extraction and invest in domestic processing of critical minerals to attract high-tech industries, semiconductors, and data centers. He proposes leveraging the Northeast’s renewable energy potential to attract tech firms and criticizes the critical minerals bill in Congress for loopholes and influence from Centrão-linked lobbies seeking to avoid industrial counterparties. Santos also pledges fiscal frankness inspired by Javier Milei, supporting pension reform, Central Bank autonomy, privatization of Correios, but opposing Petrobras privatization.

item.title: TSE: Nunes Marques e Mendonça cuidarão das ações relacionadas a propaganda eleitoral
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques appointed himself and Vice President André Mendonça to oversee electoral propaganda actions for the 2026 elections, alongside Minister Estela Aranha. The order mandates that preliminary injunctions, including right of reply analyses, be immediately submitted to the plenary for possible virtual voting. Electoral propaganda is considered sensitive due to issues like disinformation, attacks on voting machines, AI use, and post removals.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: Mentiu de novo, Flávio?
item.description: The Meio-Dia em Brasília program accused Flávio Bolsonaro of repeating lies tied to the Banco Master crisis and his connections with banker Daniel Vorcaro, while also covering the approval of a bill that loosens donation rules for municipalities. The segment suggests a pattern of misinformation by the lawmaker amid financial scandals involving his name.

item.title: Lula ganha fôlego na Futura/Apex e vira disputa de segundo turno contra Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Futura/Apex poll shows Lula (PT) at 43% in the first round, 6 points ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), above the margin of error. In a runoff, Lula leads 48% to 42%, increasing his lead to 5.5 points. Excluding blank and null votes, Lula reaches 52% of valid votes, suggesting a potential first-round victory.

item.title: Lula reforça dobradinha com Nísia Trindade em visita ao Rio
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva attends the swearing-in of cardiologist Roberto Kalil Filho as a full member of the National Academy of Medicine in Rio de Janeiro, alongside former Health Minister Nísia Trindade, reinforcing their political alliance. On Saturday, both will visit the new headquarters of the Technological Development Center in Health (CDTS/Fiocruz), underscoring Nísia’s legacy as the first woman to lead Fiocruz in over a century and her role in expanding its scientific capacity before becoming Health Minister. Their joint appearance signals a strengthening of Lula’s electoral base in Rio ahead of the 2026 re-election bid.

item.title: TSE reforça estrutura para análise da propaganda eleitoral nas Eleições 2026
item.description: The TSE issued a directive appointing Minister André Mendonça as an auxiliary judge for electoral propaganda analysis in the 2026 elections, serving alongside Minister Estela Aranha. Signed by TSE President Nunes Marques, the measure mandates that decisions on injunctions and right-of-reply requests be immediately referred to the full Court, including via virtual sessions, and will be subject to a plenary referendum.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia vota para barrar mudanças na Lei da Ficha Limpa
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Cármen Lúcia voted to declare unconstitutional provisions of a Complementary Law that reduced the ineligibility period under the Clean Record Law (Ficha Limpa). The judgment began in a virtual plenary session on Friday, the 22nd, in the Direct Action of Unconstitutionality (ADI) filed by the Sustainability Network. So far, only her vote has been disclosed.

item.title: Carmen Lúcia vota para derrubar mudança na Lei da Ficha Limpa que reduz prazo de inelegibilidade
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Cármem Lúcia voted to declare unconstitutional a change to the Clean Record Law that reduces the ineligibility period for ousted politicians, advocating for the restoration of prior rules. She argued the congressional amendment, signed by Lula with vetoes, weakens the law and threatens accountability. The virtual plenary judgment continues until November 29, pending votes from Flávio Dino, Cristiano Zanin, and Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Botafogo lança primeiro uniforme em parceria com a Mizuno; veja fotos
item.description: Botafogo unveiled its first uniform in partnership with Mizuno for the 2026/27 season, drawing inspiration from 1940s designs and featuring commemorative patches honoring the 1942 merger and 1904 founding. The black-and-white and white kits were revealed, blending historical elements with modern technology. The uniform will debut in the upcoming match against São Paulo in the Brazilian Championship.

item.title: Crusoé: Maioria não acha que áudios mudam opinião sobre Flávio, indica Futura/Apex
item.description: A Futura/Apex poll reveals that 71.5% of respondents believe the leaked audio messages from Flávio Bolsonaro to banker Daniel Vorcaro did not change their opinion of the PL presidential pre-candidate. Only 18.7% said the conversations negatively affected their perception. The findings suggest limited electoral impact from the audio scandal.

item.title: STF julga programa de escolas cívico-militares de Tarcísio
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) resumes the judgment of direct actions of unconstitutionality against the law that established the civic-military schools program in the state of São Paulo, signed by Governor Tarcísio de Freitas. The vote, under the rapporteurship of Minister Gilmar Mendes, takes place in the virtual plenary and ends on May 29, 2026. The plaintiffs (PSOL and PT) argue that the law invades the Union's exclusive competence in education and allows the discretionary replacement of tenured teachers by military personnel.

item.title: Suplente de Alcolumbre é indiciado pela PF em investigação sobre fraudes em licitações de R$ 60 mi
item.description: A substitute for Senate President Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil - AP) has been indicted by the Federal Police in an investigation into suspected fraud in DNIT procurement contracts in Amapá, involving R$ 60 million. The probe is part of a broader scheme concerning fraudulent public contracts in transportation infrastructure.

item.title: Lei garante acesso de crianças e adolescentes à saúde mental no SUS
item.description: Law 15.413/2026 guarantees universal access to mental health services in the SUS for children and adolescents, including prevention, treatment, free medication, and professional training. The law amends the Child and Adolescent Statute to include basic and specialized psychosocial care, emergency and urgent care, and hospital care. Signed by President Lula without vetoes, it originated from Bill 4.928/2023 by Senator Damares Alves and aims to combat high suicide and mental health disorder rates among Brazilian youth.

item.title: Sancionada Semana Nacional de Promoção da Pesca Artesanal
item.description: President Lula signed Law 15.414/2026, establishing the National Week for the Promotion of Artisanal Fishing, celebrated annually during the week of June 29 in honor of Saint Peter. The law aims to valorize artisanal fishing, raise awareness about its importance for food security, and encourage public policies supporting the sector and its value chain, preserving traditional knowledge and promoting environmental sustainability.

item.title: Pix é do Temer, Master é de todos
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro appeared at a rally in Florianópolis wearing a shirt that read 'Pix is Bolsonaro’s, Master is the PT’s', sparking a political debate over the origins of Brazil’s Pix payment system and the ownership of Mastercard. The statement sought to credit the Bolsonaro government with Pix while blaming the PT for Mastercard’s influence, despite Pix being launched by the Central Bank in 2020 under Bolsonaro’s administration. The reference to 'Jim Caviezel in a wig' implies a distorted or caricatured perception of current political reality.

item.title: Datafolha de hoje tem teste decisivo para Flávio e primeira simulação com Michelle
item.description: Today's Datafolha poll will be the first major electoral test following the audio leak in which Flávio Bolsonaro demanded money from banker Daniel Vorcaro to fund the Dark Horse film, measuring the scandal's impact on his presidential viability. It will also include Michelle Bolsonaro in simulated presidential scenarios for the first time, assessing her potential to unify the conservative electorate amid Flávio's declining standing. The survey, conducted March 20-22 among 2,004 voters, has a two-point margin of error.

item.title: Dólar hoje: Datafolha, BC no câmbio e exterior positivo entram no radar do mercado
item.description: The dollar is trading higher this Friday as markets await the Datafolha poll, which may reveal the political impact of the scandal involving Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro on electoral risk perception. The Central Bank is conducting a up to US$1 billion liquidity auction to support the foreign exchange market, while investors also watch the economic team’s briefing and Lula’s interview on Sem Censura. Abroad, the environment remains risk-on, with global equities rising on hopes of progress in US-Iran talks and continued strength in tech stocks.

item.title: Vídeo: Congresso derruba veto que beneficia municípios inadimplentes de até 65 mil habitantes
item.description: The National Congress overturned four provisions of the presidential veto to the 2026 Budget Guidelines Law (LDO), allowing approximately 3,000 defaulting municipalities with up to 65,000 inhabitants to regain access to federal funds, parliamentary amendments, and agreements with the Union. The revised text is now headed for promulgation. This decision benefits mayors of smaller cities that rely on voluntary transfers for local investments.

item.title: Charge do JCaesar: 22 de maio
item.description: The JCaesar cartoon published on May 22, 2026, satirizes the figure of Jair Bolsonaro, using political humor to comment on his continued presence in Brazil's electoral landscape. The illustration, published in VEJA, reflects the critical and ironic tone common in political cartoons surrounding controversial right-wing figures.

item.title: 48% rejeitam votar em Lula e 41% em Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: A Gerp poll released on May 22, 2026, shows 48% of Brazilian voters reject voting for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), while 41% reject voting for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ). The survey, conducted between May 18–21 among 2,000 voters, has a 2.24-point margin of error and 95.5% confidence level. The study was self-funded by the firm and registered with the TSE under BR-07971-2026.

item.title: Lula é desaprovado por 51% e aprovado por 41%, diz Gerp
item.description: A Gerp poll released on May 22, 2026 shows 51% of respondents disapprove and 41% approve of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's government. Evaluation of the administration shows 37% rating it as excellent/good, 15% as fair, and 47% as poor/very poor. The survey interviewed 2,000 voters from May 18–21, with a margin of error of 2.24 percentage points and a 95.5% confidence level.

item.title: Lula tem 42,7% contra 35,6% de Flávio no 1º turno, diz Futura
item.description: The Futura poll from May 2026 shows Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva leading with 42.7% of voting intentions in the first round, against 35.6% for Flávio Bolsonaro. Conducted between May 15 and 20 with 2,000 respondents and a margin of error of 2.2 percentage points, the survey also indicates Lula wins all tested second-round scenarios. Both candidates show high and nearly identical rejection rates: 44.3% for Lula and 44.7% for Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Pesquisa Apex/Futura mostra queda de 4,7 pontos de Flávio e liderança de Lula
item.description: The Apex/Futura poll released on Friday (22) shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) dropping 4.7 percentage points in the second-round simulation against Lula (PT), compared to the May 11 survey. Former president Lula maintains his lead in the 2026 electoral race.

item.title: Quase 70% dos endividados dizem acreditar que vão se beneficiar com o Desenrola 2, diz Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha survey shows 68% of indebted Brazilians believe they will personally benefit from Desenrola Brasil 2.0, while 73% see positive economic impacts overall. Optimism is highest among Lula voters (64%), young people, Northeastern residents, and low-income groups. Although public support for the program exceeds approval of Lula’s government (31% rating it excellent/good), economists warn it could overstimulate consumption and hinder the central bank’s ability to cut interest rates.

item.title: Crusoé: O voto de chuteiras
item.description: Brazil is debating Carlo Ancelotti's call-up of Neymar Jr. for the World Cup, notably omitting any comment from President Lula, who usually weighs in on many topics. While Bolsonaro supporters celebrate the selection, Lula's silence stands out.

item.title: Gritos, socos na mesa e dedo na cara… A saída caótica de Marcelão do QG de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Marcello Lopes, known as Marcelão, was fired from his role as communications chief for Flávio Bolsonaro’s pre-campaign after a chaotic outburst at the campaign headquarters in Brasília, during which he shouted, punched a glass table, pointed fingers at staff, and threatened colleagues he believed had leaked damaging information. His removal followed pressure from the PL party leadership, and despite his claim that he resigned, allies confirm he was dismissed. He will be replaced by Eduardo Fischer.

item.title: Campanhas de Lula e Flávio avaliam que rejeição de delação de Vorcaro pela PF pode reduzir tensão, mas creem em desdobramentos até a eleição
item.description: Allies of Lula's and Flávio Bolsonaro's campaigns believe the Federal Police's rejection of Daniel Vorcaro's plea deal reduces the immediate risk of escalation in the Master scandal, though they acknowledge the case could still produce developments before the election. Both sides hope the PGR will also reject the deal, limiting political fallout, but remain vigilant about potential new revelations involving other figures. While tensions have eased, the issue remains a possible source of instability in the electoral race.

item.title: De Neymar a detergente: como a polarização contaminou os mais variados assuntos do país
item.description: Neymar's call-up to the Brazilian national team sparked polarized opinions along political lines: right-wing and Bolsonaro supporters largely favored his inclusion, while left-wing and Lula supporters were mostly opposed. This episode illustrates how political polarization has invaded even seemingly non-political spheres, such as football, turning technical decisions into ideological conflicts.

item.title: Direita em crise
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro faces a credibility crisis following revelations of suspicious transactions with former banker Daniel Vorcaro, involving the receipt of 61 million reais from a U.S.-based fund. Despite damage control efforts by the Liberal Party, allies remain unconvinced and speculate about his potential withdrawal from the presidential race to run for Senate re-election in Rio de Janeiro. Jair Bolsonaro vetoed his son’s resignation and rejected Michelle Bolsonaro as a substitute, leaving the candidacy’s future uncertain.

item.title: Lula vai à posse de Roberto Kalil na Academia de Medicina
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) will travel to Rio de Janeiro on Friday, May 22, 2026, to attend the inauguration ceremony of cardiologist Roberto Kalil Filho at the National Academy of Medicine (ANM). Kalil, who is Lula’s personal physician, will assume chair number one at the institution, marking the first time in the ANM’s century-long history that a sitting Brazilian president has presided over the induction of an academic. The event will also feature Vice President Geraldo Alckmin, Health Minister Alexandre Padilha, Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes, Rio Mayor Eduardo Paes, and interim Rio Governor Ricardo Couto.

item.title: Projeto aprovado dificulta cobrança de dívidas de partidos após fusões
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved a bill that weakens debt collection mechanisms for political parties, shielding parties formed through mergers or incorporations from asset freezes and liens tied to prior debts. The law also bars automatic penalties on national directories for infractions by state or local units, applies retroactively to ongoing cases, and exposes judges who order blocked payments to liability for abuse of authority.

item.title: Eletrocardiograma eleitoral
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian presidential elections exhibit high volatility, resembling an altered electrocardiogram, with sharp swings in voter sentiment driven by scandals and leaks. Lula remains the frontrunner, but his position relies more on opposition mistakes than on his own strengths, amid high rejection, economic difficulties, and an aging narrative. Flávio Bolsonaro experienced quiet growth and even led in some second-round projections, but was severely damaged by revelations about the controversial financing of his father’s biopic by former banker Daniel Vorcaro, which inflicted substantial harm on his campaign.

item.title: Camilo Santana: “O povo quer mais”
item.description: Camilo Santana, former Education Minister and PT leader in the Northeast, says voters now seek consumer goods like smartphones and food delivery apps, reflecting shifted priorities after the Lula era's social gains. He attributes Lula’s low approval to high expectations from past administrations, slow recovery of social programs, and the spread of misinformation, urging humility and better communication. Santana also emphasizes his strategic role in preserving PT dominance in Ceará against Ciro Gomes and supporting Lula’s 2026 re-election bid.

item.title: Quando éramos reis: os bastidores da nova série da Netflix ‘Brasil 70: a Saga do Tri’
item.description: The Netflix miniseries 'Brasil 70: A Saga do Tri' portrays Brazil's historic 1970 World Cup victory, highlighting behind-the-scenes filming at Estádio Niterói and the symbolic intent to revive national pride amid uncertainty surrounding the current team ahead of the 2026 World Cup. The production aims to rekindle patriotic fervor and the magic of Zagallo’s squad — Pelé, Jairzinho, Rivellino and others — as an antidote to modern fan skepticism.

item.title: Carta ao Leitor: Torcida polarizada
item.description: Political polarization in Brazil has spread to football and public health, as seen in the divided reaction to Neymar's potential 2026 World Cup call-up and the controversy over the Ypê detergent ban, which was perceived as political retaliation due to the manufacturer's past donations to Bolsonaro's campaigns. The debate lacks evidence-based arguments and is dominated by accusations and online shouting, reflecting a deeply fractured society.

item.title: Teia de suspeitas sobre relação com Master põe candidatura de Flávio em risco
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro lost ground in polls after being implicated in the Banco Master scandal, where he sought financial aid from Daniel Vorcaro, accused of a multi-billion fraud. The gap between Lula and Flávio in the first-round simulation widened from 7 to nearly 13 points in May, according to AtlasIntel/Bloomberg, though the opposition challenges the poll’s validity due to the inclusion of the audio. Despite the decline, Lula maintains high rejection, signaling a polarized and uncertain election.

item.title: Cronologia da grana de Vorcaro alimenta suspeitas sobre a conspirata de Eduardo Bolsonaro nos EUA
item.description: Brazilian authorities are investigating whether funds from banker Daniel Vorcaro, intended for a film about Jair Bolsonaro, were used to finance Eduardo Bolsonaro's activities in the U.S. aimed at securing judicial relief for his father. A request has been filed at the STF seeking legal cooperation from the U.S. to trace the funds, following revelations of a $2 million transfer in February 2025 to a fund controlled by Eduardo's lawyer. The case may escalate from electoral damage to a criminal investigation, depending on the final use of the money.

item.title: A reunião com Cunha e Motta às vésperas do julgamento da Ficha Limpa no STF
item.description: The STF begins ruling this Friday on a case challenging amendments to the Clean Record Law, which could redefine eligibility rules for the 2026 elections. The decision may determine who is allowed to run, creating significant political anticipation. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Julgamento do STF sobre Lei da Ficha Limpa pode beneficiar Cunha, Garotinho e Arruda; leia bastidor
item.description: The STF is set to rule on Friday on congressional changes to the Clean Record Law that reduce the period of ineligibility for convicted politicians. While rapporteur Minister Cármen Lúcia is expected to defend the original law, there is anticipation that the Court may uphold part of the congressional amendments, benefiting figures such as Eduardo Cunha, Anthony Garotinho, and José Roberto Arruda. A compromise or request for vista could temporarily preserve the rules favorable to politicians with criminal records.

item.title: ‘Pai’ da Ficha Limpa: STF pode beneficiar crime organizado se validar lei aprovada no Congresso
item.description: Márlon Reis, the creator of the Clean Record Law, warns that if the Supreme Federal Court validates a congressional law reducing the ineligibility period for convicted politicians, it will benefit organized crime by allowing individuals involved in serious crimes, such as latrocínio, to run for office. The law, passed in September, limits ineligibility to eight years from the conviction date — not the end of a revoked mandate — favoring figures like Eduardo Cunha, José Roberto Arruda, and Anthony Garotinho. The STF begins judging the action this Friday, with rapporteur Minister Cármen Lúcia.

item.title: Quando a exceção vira regra: a liminar monocrática no controle abstrato do STF
item.description: The STF has increasingly relied on monocratic injunctions to suspend laws in abstract constitutional control, despite constitutional and statutory provisions reserving such decisions for the plenary. Although the plenary referendum required by Law 9.868/1999 never occurred in the case of EC 73/2013, the practice has become entrenched, as seen in the suspension of the Dosimetry Law (15.402/2026) by Alexandre de Moraes, producing a cautionary effect without effective collegial oversight. This reveals a silent mutation in constitutional review: the collegial form is preserved, but its deliberative function is hollowed out by individual decisions followed by formal ad referendum validation.

item.title: Escândalo do Master trava pacificação entre Michelle e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The release of audio messages in which Flávio Bolsonaro demanded money from banker Daniel Vorcaro to fund the 'Dark Horse' project disrupted efforts to reconcile him with former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro, creating internal tension within the Bolsonaro clan. While not directly impacting the pre-presidential campaign, the scandal exposed personal and financial divisions within the family's political circle.

item.title: 'Timing do escândalo com Vorcaro foi bom para Flávio Bolsonaro, dará tempo de se recuperar', diz Marcos Nobre
item.description: Philosopher and political scientist Marcos Nobre argues that the scandal involving Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro will not harm his 2026 presidential campaign, as the timing of the revelation gives him time to recover before October. He notes that Flávio leads a coalition of traditional and radical right seeking to halt income redistribution policies since 2018, and that despite his ties to Vorcaro, his candidacy remains competitive. Nobre also observes that President Lula struggles to mediate wealth distribution conflicts, having turned to confrontation with Congress in his current term.

item.title: Datafolha divulga nesta sexta nova pesquisa sobre eleição presidencial
item.description: Datafolha releases a new presidential election poll for 2026 this Friday (22), presenting voting intentions for both rounds, candidate rejection rates, and public evaluation of Lula’s government. The survey aims to map the current electoral landscape, focusing on voter perception of leading candidates and the Petrobras administration.

item.title: Lula reforça equipe de cúpula da pré-campanha de olho na crise de Flávio
item.description: Lula and the PT have strengthened their pre-campaign team with Eden Valadares and Laércio Ribeiro to counter the crisis facing Flávio Bolsonaro, who is under scrutiny due to his ties with Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master. The party has launched a digital war strategy, aiming to label the senator a 'liar,' while investing in boosting its online presence, a domain traditionally dominated by the far-right.

item.title: Com derrubada de veto de Lula, Congresso libera doação antes das eleições e reforça caixa de aliados em redutos
item.description: Congress overturned Lula's vetoes on the Budget Guidelines Law (LDO), releasing federal transfers to municipalities ahead of the 2026 elections, easing the execution of amendments and boosting allies' funds in electoral strongholds. The measure, passed with broad party support, contradicted legislative technical advice and was backed by government allies and the PT.

item.title: Cúpula do PL vê urgência de segurar palanques e garantir eleição das bancadas em meio à crise com Flávio
item.description: The PL leadership now prioritizes preserving competitive state-level electoral bases and securing large congressional delegations (30 senators and 120 deputies) amid the crisis involving Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and Banco Master. The party fears the national scandal could taint proportional candidacies and regional alliances, undermining its institutional strength. Although Flávio’s presidential candidacy is still publicly defended, internal caution is growing, with allies reconsidering support due to risks of new revelations.
